operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case identifiers everywhere (Aircraft_ID, Pilot_name, Order_Year); must double-quote with original spelling.
DDL uses backtick-quoted FK refs (`pilot`(`Pilot_ID`)) inside CREATE TABLE; sqlite_master text must be replayed verbatim.
pilot_record PK is composite (Pilot_ID, Aircraft_ID, Date) with Date TEXT — composite-PK member gets max_l0=30, not inf.
Date column is TEXT storage but semantically a date 'YYYY/MM/DD'; declared type TEXT dispatches to String fuzzer, not Date.
Order_Year / Join_Year are INT declared, dispatch to Number (not Year fuzzer) — no 'year' substring in type.
All columns notnull=0, no CHECK, no UNIQUE indexes: nothing enforced at insert; only PK/FK constraints bite.
FKs point to existing parents with unique PKs (aircraft.Aircraft_ID, pilot.Pilot_ID) — no dangling/non-unique parents here.
Tiny tables (7/5/6 rows): original_values lists are short; rng.choices(k=min(5,len)) will reuse nearly all originals.
pilot_record has Record_ID INT not in PK and not unique — TS will happily duplicate it.
No self-references, no views/triggers/indexes beyond PKs.
Pilot_name contains apostrophes (O'Bryant, O'Neal) — literal quoting must double them if ever emitted.
Fleet_Series / Model contain parentheses and spaces — String fuzzer CHARSET includes () and space, so contamination plausible.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on Aircraft_ID/Pilot_ID/Record_ID: range [-10^0,10^0] default scale, then +-1/+-2 perturbation; PKs will collide often, sample_fresh_primary_keys drops duplicates.
Order_Year/Join_Year/Rank/Age as Number: fresh draws uniform in [-1,1] (scale 0) — implausible years/ages, likely FN on range predicates.
Date column via String fuzzer: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings, not 'YYYY/MM/DD' — any date-format predicate will miss (FN).
String fuzzer on Manufacturer/Model/Powertrain: 20-char random strings + 50% contaminate; original 2-7 distinct values rarely reproduced.

pilot_record FK columns draw from parent FINAL filtered values with replacement — many duplicate (Pilot_ID,Aircraft_ID) pairs, Date random string makes PK collisions rare, so composite PK rarely filtered.
Number list-range quirk (list_max overwritten to full max) means even with elements, fresh draws dominate when rng<p.
p=0.2 default, whole-instance p=0 w.p. 0.3: 30% of instances are pure element-reuse (near-original values), 70% heavily fresh.
max_l0 cap (rng*30) on non-PK columns: after ~30 fresh draws values repeat, creating ties the original lacks (FP risk on DISTINCT/COUNT).
Tiny originals (5-7 rows) mean element pool is small; String/Number samplers will over-represent the few originals when p small.
No NOT NULL/CHECK: NULLs never inserted by TS (samplers drop None), so IS NULL predicates always false — FN.
FK consistency holds (parents exist), so join predicates on Pilot_ID/Aircraft_ID will match; but Date join across tables unlikely.
